Title: GET /api/v1/reports/overdue returns 500 whenever the report contains rows
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / test DB .data/taskflow.test.db
StepsToReproduce: 1. Login as owner@example.com. 2. GET /api/v1/reports/overdue. 3. Observe the server console.
ExpectedResult: 200 with count, byProject and the overdue task rows.
ActualResult: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR; server log: 'no such column: ua.display_name'.
DetectedBy: Manual API smoke test (curl/node fetch) before suite authoring
Evidence: Fixed & retested: test-reports/playwright/api.json (TASK-TC-042 @smoke pass); raw logs in test-evidence/logs/
RootCause: The rows query selected ua.display_name while the shared FROM clause did not join users.
RegressionResult: Pass - reports suite green in every subsequent full run
Rationale: Found on first contact with the endpoint; would have been a hard 500 in the demo. Added the assignee LEFT JOIN only to the rows query (count/byProject do not need it).

Title: Seed data due-date offsets were sign-inverted (negative offsets landed in the future)
StepsToReproduce: 1. npm run db:reset. 2. Inspect tasks.due_date in SQLite. 3. Compare with the documented fixture intent (3 overdue, 1 due today).
ExpectedResult: Three tasks due in the past and exactly one due today; overdue report count 3 for the owner.
ActualResult: Tasks configured as '-3 days' were stored 3 days in the FUTURE; the overdue filter matched the wrong rows (e.g. OPS tasks appeared overdue).
DetectedBy: SQL cross-check during exploration charter TASK-EXP-003
Evidence: Fixed & retested: db:reset shows 3 overdue + 1 due-today; test-reports/db-results.json (TASK-TC-205) green
RootCause: seedDatabase passed dueDays directly to seedDate(daysAgo), inverting the sign of every relative offset.
RegressionResult: Pass - DB checks re-derive the rule and stay green after reset
Rationale: Fixture data that contradicts its own documentation is worse than no fixture; caught by comparing the DB against the stated expectations rather than trusting the report output.

Title: GET /api/v1/projects returned an empty data array (total was correct) for every user
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / test DB
StepsToReproduce: 1. Login as owner. 2. POST a project (201). 3. GET /api/v1/projects?limit=100. 4. Observe data=[] while total>=3. 5. Repeat for the seeded owner: the list is empty too.
ExpectedResult: The authenticated user's projects are returned in data with a matching X-Total-Count.
ActualResult: data was always [] (X-Total-Count and total were correct) because the route's WHERE repeated the user filter that PROJECT_SELECT already binds, shifting values into the LIMIT/OFFSET placeholders.
Evidence: Fixed & retested: test-reports/playwright/api.json (TASK-TC-006/008/048 pass); isolated SQL probe confirmed under-bound statements silently carry NULL into WHERE
RootCause: Duplicate bind parameter: PROJECT_SELECT contains 'pm.user_id = ?' in the JOIN and the route added another; node:sqlite does not throw on missing values, it leaves placeholders NULL.
RegressionResult: Pass - project list assertions green in the full run; UI project switcher populated
Rationale: The most instructive defect of the build: same-family SQL mistakes can return plausible-looking totals with silently empty payloads, so count+payload parity is now asserted in the DB suite too.

Title: Console was served from the wrong static directory (404 'Not found' on /)
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / Playwright Chromium
StepsToReproduce: 1. Start the server. 2. GET /. 3. Observe the plain 'Not found' page.
ExpectedResult: The login console is served from app/public.
ActualResult: PUBLIC_DIR resolved to app/server/public (does not exist), so every UI test failed at page load; screenshot showed 'Not found'.
DetectedBy: Automated UI suite (first UI run, all 10 tests failed at page load)
Evidence: Fixed & retested: test-evidence/screenshots/login-1440x900.jpg captured from the running app; UI suite green
RootCause: path.resolve(HERE, '..', 'public') missed one directory level (app/server/src -> app/public needs two).
RegressionResult: Pass - full UI suite green incl. mobile screenshots
Rationale: Found because the UI suite exercises the real server rather than a mock; a mocked API layer would never have caught it.

Title: Hidden modal backdrop intercepted all clicks (login unusable)
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / Playwright Chromium
StepsToReproduce: 1. Open the console in a browser. 2. Try to click or tab to the login button. 3. Observe clicks hitting an invisible element.
ExpectedResult: The hidden modal backdrop is not rendered/interactive; login fields are clickable.
ActualResult: Playwright click on #login-submit was intercepted forever by <div hidden class='modal-backdrop'> because .modal-backdrop { display: grid } overrode the hidden attribute.
DetectedBy: Automated UI suite (interception logs in the click retry call log)
Evidence: Fixed & retested: global [hidden] { display: none !important; } in styles.css; UI suite green
RootCause: Classic CSS vs hidden-attribute clash: component display rules beat the UA stylesheet for [hidden].
RegressionResult: Pass - all click-driven UI tests green in the full run
Rationale: A human might have dismissed this as a rendering quirk; the automation retry log pinpointed the intercepting element and its cause.

Title: Validation error banner was not dismissible while the modal was open (rendered under the backdrop)
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / Playwright Chromium
StepsToReproduce: 1. Login. 2. Open the create-task modal. 3. Enter a 2-character title and save (400). 4. Try to click the banner's dismiss button.
ExpectedResult: The validation banner is visible above the modal and its dismiss button is clickable.
ActualResult: The banner rendered behind the fixed backdrop; the dismiss click retried until timeout.
DetectedBy: Automated UI suite (TASK-TC-106 timed out clicking error-dismiss)
Evidence: Fixed & retested: .error-banner raised with position:relative + z-index:100; TASK-TC-106 green
RootCause: Stacking context: backdrop is position:fixed with z-index:50, banner had no z-index/position.
RegressionResult: Pass - validation banner test green; screenshot validation-error-1440x900.jpg shows the banner over the modal
Rationale: Kept the banner as the single error surface (requirement) and fixed the layering instead of moving errors inside the modal.

Title: [SEEDED] Overdue predicate uses <= so tasks due today are reported overdue
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / own DB .data/taskflow.seeded.db
StepsToReproduce: 1. SEED_DEFECTS=1 npm run start. 2. Login as owner. 3. GET /api/v1/reports/overdue.
ExpectedResult: count = 3 (tasks due today are NOT overdue per business rule 7).
ActualResult: count = 4 with the due-today task leaked into the list.
DetectedBy: Injected on purpose; detection demonstrated by npm run seeded:demo
RetestResult: Pass - default runs keep SEED_DEFECTS=0 and report count 3
RegressionResult: Pass - TASK-TC-042/205 and the demo both detect the injected behaviour
Rationale: Labelled SEEDED everywhere; exists to prove the suite detects a realistic off-by-one business-rule bug.

Title: [SEEDED] DONE is not terminal: DONE -> IN_PROGRESS is accepted
Environment: Local Windows 11 / Node v24 / own DB .data/taskflow.seeded.db
StepsToReproduce: 1. SEED_DEFECTS=1 npm run start. 2. Drive a task to DONE. 3. PATCH /tasks/:id/status {status:'IN_PROGRESS'}.
ActualResult: 200 and the task moves back to IN_PROGRESS.
DetectedBy: Injected on purpose; detection demonstrated by npm run seeded:demo
RootCause: getAllowedTransitions() returns ['IN_PROGRESS'] for DONE when SEED_DEFECTS=1.
RegressionResult: Pass - TASK-TC-028 and the demo both detect the injected behaviour
Rationale: Labelled SEEDED everywhere; proves the transition suite catches a broken terminal state.
